IRS990.MissionDesc: Point Loma Nazarene University exists to provide higher education in a vital Christian community where minds are engaged and challenged, character is modeled and formed, and service becomes an expression of faith. We aspire to be a learning community where grace is foundational, truth is pursued, and holiness is a way of life.
IRS990.Desc: Instructional activities, including student aid, prepare students to address the complex issues facing our world today with integrity and forward thinking. PLNU graduates enter the workforce prepared to influence our world for good. PLNU serves more than 4,400 students offering more than 50 undergraduate areas of study and 12 graduate programs throughout Southern California.

ProgSrvcAccomActy2Grp.Desc: Student Services enriches the student experience and resources like the Offices of Strengths and Vocation, the Wellness Center, Outdoor Leadership and Recreation, Spiritual Development, and Student Financial Services.

ProgSrvcAccomActy3Grp.Desc: Academic Support bolsters PLNU students' academic experience through resources like the Tutorial Center, PLNU's Ryan Library, Information Technology Services, and Media and Technology.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Schedule I, Part I, Line 2 Procedures for monitoring use of grant funds.
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The University awards grants, scholarships, and student loans based on various predefined criteria. Students must qualify for the assistance. Student enrollment and continuing eligibility are verified on an ongoing basis. Amounts are applied directly to student accounts, and no cash changes hands.

This is not included in taxable compensation. The VP for University Services met the qualifications for and received a ministerial housing allowance during the tax year.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Schedule J, Part I, Line 1a Payments for business use of personal residence
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The University reimburses Dr. Brower, President, for the cost of house cleaning or landscaping expenses when his residence is used for University business. These amounts are not included in taxable income.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Schedule J, Part I, Line 7 Non-fixed payments

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 15 Process for determining compensation
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: EACH YEAR AT THE SPRING BOARD MEETING OF THE UNIVERSITY'S BOARD OF TRUSTEES, THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE OF THE BOARD RECEIVES A REPORT IN EXECUTIVE SESSION FROM THE ASSOCIATE VICE PRESIDENT FOR HUMAN RESOURCES WHICH COMPARES THE SALARIES OF THE UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT AND SENIOR ADMINISTRATORS (THE ADMINISTRATIVE CABINET) TO SALARIES FOR SIMILAR POSITIONS USING FOUR DIFFERENT SALARY SURVEYS. FOLLOWING DISCUSSION OF THIS INFORMATION, THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE TAKES ACTION TO SET THE SALARIES OF THE PRESIDENT AND ADMINISTRATIVE CABINET FOR THE FOLLOWING YEAR, SUBJECT TO APPROVAL OF THE FULL BOARD, AND RECORDS THIS ACTION IN THE MINUTES OF ITS MEETING.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 1a Executive Committee:
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The governing board has an Executive Committee which, with several specific exceptions, has the authority to act for the board on all matters should the Executive Committee determine that it would be imprudent to wait for the next board meeting to take action. The committee is composed of the chairs of the standing committees (except for the audit and risk management committees), the University President, the President of the PLNU Foundation, and the officers of the board (the Chair, Vice Chair, and Secretary.) The board, through its policy manual and various adopted resolutions, has delegated specific levels of responsibility and authority to the University President in order to enable him and others at the University to make timely operational decisions. The President works with an administrative cabinet that has been hired by the President and approved by the board in carrying out his delegated responsibilities and in operating the University on a day to day basis. The President's Cabinet consists of Robert Brower, President; Joe LaLuzerne, Chief Financial Officer; Kerry Fulcher, Provost; Mary Paul, Vice President for Student Life and Formation; Jeff Bolster, Vice President for University Services; and Kelly Smith, Vice President for University Advancement.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 11b Review of form 990 by governing body
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Form 990 is prepared by an independent CPA firm, reviewed in detail by the finance team, and distributed to the board of trustees prior to being filed with the IRS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 12c Conflict of interest policy
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Conflict of interest statements are completed annually by all members of the governing body, as well as officers and key employees. The statements are reviewed by the Chairman of the Audit Committee of the Board of Trustees. The finance team also monitors all transactions for potential conflicts of interest. Should any potential conflicts of interest be disclosed, the board member or officer would be asked to refrain from participation in any deliberation or decision with regard to matters affected by the relationship.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 19 Required documents available to the public
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The organizing documents, conflict of interest policy, and the financial statements are available upon request.
